title: EgressEvent
description: One call that actually happened, recorded by a runtime hook. Where a declared egress point says the code can reach a provider, an event says it did.
$comment: The hook records the shape of a payload and never its content. A tool that exists to stop data leaving must not become the thing that copies it. Transport is fixed here as well: a hook appends one JSON object per line to a file ending in .jsonl inside the directory named by PERISKOP_EVENT_DIR, one file per process. Line delimited append is chosen because a partially written last line costs one event rather than corrupting the file, and because two processes appending never need a lock.

egress_event_id.description: Deterministic, derived from the call shape rather than from a counter, so the same call recorded twice carries one identity. The derivation is normative and every hook must apply it identically: blake3 over the domain tag ee/v1 followed by library.module, operation, target.host_id and target.path_template, each composed to Unicode NFC and encoded as UTF-8, each separated by byte 0x1f, an absent field written as the empty string, rendered as ee_ plus the first eight bytes in lowercase hex. Two hooks that derive it differently would give one call two identities and defeat deduplication, which is why this is fixed in the contract rather than left to each implementation. NFC is part of the derivation and not an afterthought: one visible name can be written as several byte sequences, so a module or host spelled with a composed accent and the same name spelled with a combining one would derive two identities for one call, and nothing would reject either record. The domain tag itself is not normalised; it is a literal fixed by this contract.

runtime.description: Interpreter and version, for example cpython/3.12 or node/20.

entrypoint_hint.description: Best effort name of what is running, and a bare name rather than a path: the pattern rejects every path separator, not only a leading one. The sentence "never an absolute path" stood here alone for four revisions while nothing enforced it, so a hook launched with PERISKOP_HOOK_ENTRYPOINT=/srv/app/worker.py wrote one machine's deployment layout into every event it recorded, and the validator passed the record. Both hooks already reduce the value to a basename, which means the rule cost them nothing and was upheld only by their courtesy; a third producer had no reason to guess it. Three consequences, each sufficient on its own. An absolute path makes the same run on two machines stop producing byte identical output, which is what the report format rests on. It copies a home or deployment directory into a record that gets archived and shared. And the hint is a display name a reader groups events by, so a rooted one is a distinct group per host for what is one service. Windows drive prefixes are rejected as well, since the process that wrote the record need not have run the operating system of the one reading it.

module.description: Package the call went through, for example openai or httpx.

mechanism.description: Which layer the hook sat at. An sdk_wrapper observation is stronger evidence than an http_client one, because the latter cannot tell a provider call from any other request without the target.

operation.description: Method or endpoint that was invoked, normalised to lower case.

host_id.description: Destination host. Recorded as written, since a scan needs to compare it against what the code declared.

path_template.description: Request path with identifiers removed, so two calls to the same endpoint compare equal.

provider_ref.description: Classified provider, or unknown. Never omitted to hide an unclassified destination.

payload_shape.description: Structure of what was sent. Content is not recorded and cannot be recovered from these fields.

field_paths.description: Normalised field paths, sorted. Dynamic keys are replaced by a placeholder, because a key can carry data as readily as a value: a map keyed by customer email would otherwise copy those addresses into the record.

byte_size_estimate.description: Approximate size of the request body, in bytes. An estimate rather than a measurement, since materialising a streaming body to weigh it would change the behaviour of the program under observation. The derivation is normative and no producer may choose its own, because the value is not carried by the identity: two hooks that weighed one call differently would write two records under one egress_event_id, and the collector keeps whichever sorted first, so the number a report shows would depend on which language happened to be observed. Exactly one of three bases is used, in this precedence, and the first that applies wins. (1) A byte count the caller or the transport already stated for this body: a content-length, a declared length, or the length of the buffer the body arrived as. It is preferred over everything else because it is the only basis that reports the bytes that actually left. (2) The summed length of the pieces seen on the way out, when the body left in parts and was counted without being reassembled. (3) A structural estimate over the walked payload, used only when the body has not been serialised yet and no length exists to read: each scalar counts 8 bytes, each null counts 4, each string counts its length in bytes, and sampled sequences are counted over the sampled elements only, with the same ceilings the field path walk uses. A basis 3 number is a lower bound on a body that has not been encoded; it is not comparable with a basis 1 number for the same call, and a consumer comparing sizes across producers must treat a difference as a difference of basis before treating it as a difference of traffic. Zero means the body carried nothing, never that nothing could be weighed: a body that could not be measured at all is declared through the degraded reason vocabulary instead.

truncated_depth.description: Depth at which traversal stopped. Present so a shallow record is not mistaken for a small payload.

call_site_hint.description: Best effort link back to source. Advisory only: reconciliation joins on the call shape, not on this.

path.description: Relative to the project root. Absolute paths are rejected.

degraded_reasons.description: Why this record is less complete than a full one. Present so a thin event is read as thin rather than as evidence of a small call.
